assessment.name: Children’s Eating Attitudes Test (ChEAT)
assessment.description: The Children’s Eating Attitudes Test (ChEAT) is a 26 item questionnaire used to assess eating attitudes and disordered eating behaviours in children aged 8 to 15. For younger children it is administered by orally reading items to the child, while adolescents can self-report responses. It is a modified version of the Eating Attitudes Test (Garner & Garfinkle, 1979)

source_rule_excerpts: Items are summed to obtain a total score. A cut-off score of 20 more indicates the presence of disturbed eating patterns and highlights the need for further assessment (Garner et l., 1982). A total score of 20 corresponds to an average score of 0.77.
Average scores between 0 and 3 are computed by dividing the raw score by the number of questions, and are presented for each of the four subscales.

source_guidance.title: ChEAT Scoring & Interpretation
source_guidance.text:
Items are summed to obtain a total score. A cut-off score of 20 more indicates the presence of disturbed eating patterns and highlights the need for further assessment (Garner et l., 1982). A total score of 20 corresponds to an average score of 0.77.
Average scores between 0 and 3 are computed by dividing the raw score by the number of questions, and are presented for each of the four subscales.
Higher scores indicate increased symptom severity. Subscales are derived by summing the following items:
Dieting : 1, 2, 6, 10,11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 22, 23, 24
Restricting and Purging : 2, 7, 9,10, 17, 22, 23, 24, 26
Food Preoccupation : 3, 4, 18, 20, 21
Oral Control: 8, 13, 15, 20
